title.en: Volume 85: Men of Letters - Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin
title.raw: 卷85 文苑：袁躍 裴敬憲 盧觀 封肅 邢臧 裴伯茂 邢昕 Volume 85: Men of Letters - Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin

sentences.zh: 袁躍 裴敬憲 盧觀 封肅 邢臧 裴伯茂 邢昕 溫子昇

translations.literal: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, Wen Zisheng
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, and Wen Zisheng

sentences.zh: 夫文之為用，其來日久。

translations.literal: As for the use of literature, its coming has been long.
translations.idiomatic: Literature has served human purposes for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 自昔聖達之作，賢哲之書，莫不統理成章，蘊氣標致，其流廣變，諸非一貫，文質推移，與時俱化。

translations.literal: From of old the works of sages and worthies and the books of the wise have all been ordered into chapters, imbued with spirit and marked by style; their currents are broad and varied and not of one tradition; substance and ornament shift and transform with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, the writings of the greatest sages and the books of the wisest minds have all been shaped into coherent form, charged with spirit and distinguished by style. Their currents spread and change in many ways rather than following a single line; elegance and plainness evolve as literature keeps pace with the times.

sentences.zh: 淳于出齊，有雕龍之目；

translations.literal: Chunyu came forth from Qi and had the eyes of the Carved Dragon;
translations.idiomatic: When Chunyu emerged from Qi, he possessed the discerning eye celebrated in the title Carving the Dragon;

sentences.zh: 靈均逐楚，著嘉禍之章。

translations.literal: Lingjun followed Chu into exile and composed the chapter of auspicious calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yuan followed Chu into exile and wrote his celebrated piece on the noble orange.

sentences.zh: [2]漢之西京，馬揚為首稱；

translations.literal: In the Western Capital of Han, Sima and Yang were foremost in renown;
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Capital of the Han, Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong were the leading names;

sentences.zh: 東都之下，班張為雄伯。

translations.literal: Under the Eastern Capital, Ban and Zhang were the heroic lords.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Eastern Capital, Ban Gu and Zhang Heng were the reigning masters.

sentences.zh: 曹植信魏世之英，陸機則晉朝之秀，雖同時並列，分途爭遠。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi was truly the hero of Wei times, and Lu Ji the outstanding talent of the Jin; though standing at the same time, they contested along separate paths to ever greater distance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi was truly the genius of the Wei, and Lu Ji the outstanding talent of the Jin; though contemporaries, they pursued diverging paths to ever greater distance.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之後，天下分崩，夷狄交馳，文章殄滅。

translations.literal: After the Yongjia era, the realm fragmented, barbarians rode in succession, and belles-lettres perished.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia turmoil, the empire fell apart, foreign peoples surged one after another, and literary culture was nearly extinguished.

sentences.zh: 昭成、太祖之世，南收燕趙，網羅俊乂。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Zhaocheng and Taizu, they gathered Yan and Zhao to the south and netted outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaocheng and Emperor Daowu, the court recovered Yan and Zhao in the south and gathered men of outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 逮高祖馭天，銳情文學，蓋以頡頏漢徹，掩踔曹丕，氣韻高豔，才藻獨構。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took Heaven's mandate, he was keen on literature, roughly rivaling Han Wudi, surpassing Cao Pi, with lofty spirit and brilliant ornament and literary talent uniquely formed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he threw himself into literature, in spirit rivaling Emperor Wu of Han and outshining Cao Pi, with a lofty tone, brilliant style, and literary gifts all his own.

sentences.zh: 衣冠仰止，咸慕新風。

translations.literal: The gentry looked up and all admired the new style.
translations.idiomatic: Men of culture looked up to him, and all were drawn to the new literary current he set.

sentences.zh: 肅宗歷位，文雅大盛，學者如牛毛，成者如麟角，孔子曰：「才難，不其然乎？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong held the throne, refinement flourished greatly; learners were like ox-hairs, achievers like unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is it not so?"
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, literary culture flourished as never before: students were as numerous as ox hairs, but those who truly succeeded were as rare as unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is that not exactly the case?"

sentences.zh: 袁躍，字景騰，陳郡人，尚書翻弟也。

translations.literal: Yuan Yue, style name Jingteng, was a man of Chen commandery and the younger brother of Minister of Works Yuan Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yue, whose style was Jingteng, came from Chen commandery and was the younger brother of Minister of Works Yuan Fan.

sentences.zh: 博學儁才，性不矯俗，篤於交友。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and outstanding in talent, by nature not given to affectation, and devoted in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely learned and exceptionally gifted, unpretentious by nature, and deeply loyal to his friends.

sentences.zh: 翻每謂人曰：「躍可謂我家千里駒也。

translations.literal: Fan often said to people, "Yue may be called the thousand-li colt of our house.
translations.idiomatic: Fan often told others, "Yue may truly be called the thousand-li steed of our clan.

sentences.zh: 」釋褐司空行參軍，歷位尚書都兵郎中，加員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " He took his first office as Acting Adjutant in the Bureau of the Minister of Works, rose through posts to Director of Arms in the Ministry of Works, and was additionally made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " He began his career as acting adjutant in the Bureau of the Minister of Works, rose to director of arms in the Ministry of Works, and was later given the additional title of supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 將立明堂，躍乃上議，當時稱其博洽。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was about to be established, Yue submitted a memorial of discussion, and at the time he was praised as broadly versed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was preparing to build the Bright Hall, Yue submitted a memorial on the subject, and contemporaries praised his encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕主阿那瓌亡破來奔，朝廷矜之，送復其國。

translations.literal: The Rouran ruler Anagui, destroyed and fleeing, came to surrender; the court took pity on him and sent him back to restore his state.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui, ruler of the Rouran, fled to the court after his state was destroyed; the court took pity on him and helped restore his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 既而每使朝貢，辭旨頗不盡禮。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever he sent tribute missions, their wording was rather lacking in courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever he sent tribute missions, their language was often less than fully respectful.

sentences.zh: 躍為朝臣書與瓌，陳以禍福，言辭甚美。

translations.literal: Yue wrote on behalf of the court ministers to Gui, setting forth fortune and calamity; the language was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Yue drafted a letter from the court ministers to Anagui, explaining the consequences of fortune and disaster in language of exceptional elegance.

sentences.zh: 後遷車騎將軍、太傅、清河王懌文學，雅為懌所愛賞。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to literary aide to the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Prince of Qinghe, Yuan Yi, and was greatly loved and rewarded by Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed literary aide to Prince Yi of Qinghe, who also held the posts of general of chariots and cavalry and grand tutor, and Yi greatly favored and admired him.

sentences.zh: 懌之文表多出於躍。

translations.literal: Yi's literary memorials and proclamations mostly came from Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Yi's official documents and memorials were written by Yue.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the titles Champion General and Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously honored as champion general and director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 所制文集行於世。

translations.literal: The collected writings he composed circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 無子，兄翻以子聿脩繼。

translations.literal: He had no son; his elder brother Fan made his son Yuxiu the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his elder brother Fan had his own son Yuxiu succeed him.

sentences.zh: 聿脩，字叔德，七歲遭喪，居處禮若成人。

translations.literal: Yuxiu, style name Shude, at age seven suffered bereavement and in deportment observed ritual like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiu, whose style was Shude, lost his father at seven and conducted himself in mourning with the propriety of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 九歲，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At nine he was summoned by the province as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he was summoned by the provincial administration as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 性深沉，有鑒識，清靖寡欲，與物無競。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and reserved, with discernment, pure and quiet with few desires, and not competitive with others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was reserved and perceptive, pure and restrained in his desires, and never contentious with others.

sentences.zh: 姨夫尚書崔休深所知賞。

translations.literal: His uncle by marriage, Minister Cui Xiu, deeply knew and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle by marriage, Minister Cui Xiu, knew him well and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 年十八，領本州中正，兼尚書度支郎中。

translations.literal: At eighteen he headed the provincial rectifier of his native commandery and concurrently served as Director of Revenue Accounts in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he served as rectifier of his native commandery and concurrently as director of revenue accounts in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，除太子庶子，以本官行博陵太守。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and acted as Administrator of Boling with his former title.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Qi received the abdication, he was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent and acted as administrator of Boling while retaining his former rank.

sentences.zh: 裴敬憲，字孝虞，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Jingxian, style name Xiaoyu, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jingxian, whose style was Xiaoyu, came from Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史宣第二子。

translations.literal: He was the second son of Xuan, Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was the second son of Xuan, governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 少有志行，學博才清，撫訓諸弟，專以讀誦為業。

translations.literal: In youth he had resolve and conduct, was broadly learned with clear talent, nurtured and instructed his younger brothers, and devoted himself solely to reading and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed purpose and integrity, was widely learned with a refined gift for letters, raised and instructed his younger brothers, and devoted himself entirely to study.

sentences.zh: 澹於榮利，風氣俊遠，郡徵功曹不就，諸府辟命，先進其弟，世人歎美之。

translations.literal: Indifferent to glory and profit, his bearing lofty and distant, he did not accept the commandery's summons as Merit Officer; when various offices summoned him, he advanced his younger brothers first, and people of the age sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Indifferent to fame and gain, with a lofty and distant manner, he declined the commandery's summons as merit officer; when various offices offered him posts, he urged his younger brothers forward first, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 司州牧、高陽王雍舉秀才，射策高第，除太學博士。

translations.literal: The Governor of Sizhou, Prince of Gaoyang, Yuan Yong, recommended him as a cultivated talent; in the archery examination he ranked at the top and was made Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yong, governor of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, recommended him as a cultivated talent; he placed at the top in the policy examination and was appointed erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 性和雅，未嘗失色於人。

translations.literal: His nature was harmonious and refined; he never lost composure before others.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament was gentle and refined; he never lost his composure in company.

sentences.zh: 工隸草，解音律，五言之作，獨擅於時。

translations.literal: He was skilled in clerical and cursive script, understood music, and in five-character verse had a monopoly on the age.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at clerical and cursive calligraphy, understood music theory, and in five-character poetry had no rival of his day.

sentences.zh: 名聲甚重，後進共宗慕之。

translations.literal: His reputation was very weighty, and younger men all took him as a model and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation was immense, and younger writers all looked up to him as a model.

sentences.zh: 中山王將之部，[3]朝賢送於河梁，賦詩言別，皆以敬憲為最。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhongshan was about to depart for his post, court worthies saw him off at River Bridge and composed parting poems; all regarded Jingxian's as the finest.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhongshan was leaving for his post, court worthies saw him off at River Bridge with parting poems; all agreed that Jingxian's was the finest.

sentences.zh: 其文不能贍逸，而有清麗之美。

translations.literal: His writing could not supply abundance and ease, yet had the beauty of clarity and elegance.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was not expansive or effortless, yet it possessed a clear, refined beauty.

sentences.zh: 少有氣病，年三十三卒，人物甚悼之。

translations.literal: From youth he had a qi disorder; he died at thirty-three, and people of the age deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He had suffered from a chronic breathing ailment since youth; he died at thirty-three, and contemporaries mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 敬憲世有仁義於鄉里。

translations.literal: Jingxian's family for generations had benevolence and righteousness in the village.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian's family had long been known in their district for benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，蜀賊陳雙熾所過殘暴，至敬憲宅，輒相約束，不得焚燒。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, the Shu bandit Chen Shuangchi was brutal wherever he passed; when he reached Jingxian's house, they mutually restrained one another and did not burn it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era, the Shu rebel Chen Shuangchi ravaged everything in his path; when he reached Jingxian's home, his men bound themselves by agreement not to set it afire.

sentences.zh: 為物所伏如此。

translations.literal: He was so submitted to by things.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the respect his moral standing commanded.

sentences.zh: 永興三年，[4]贈中書侍郎，諡曰文。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxing, he was posthumously given Vice Director of the Secretariat, posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yongxing reign, he was posthumously honored as vice director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 封肅，字元邕，勃海人，尚書回之兄子也。

translations.literal: Feng Su, style name Yuanyong, was a man of Bohai and the elder brother's son of Minister Feng Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Su, whose style was Yuanyong, came from Bohai and was the nephew of Minister Feng Hui.

sentences.zh: 早有文思，博涉經史，太傅崔光見而賞焉。

translations.literal: Early he had literary thought, broadly traversed the classics and histories, and Grand Tutor Cui Guang saw and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He showed literary talent early, ranged widely through the classics and histories, and Grand Tutor Cui Guang recognized and favored him.

sentences.zh: 位太學博士，修起居注，兼廷尉監。

translations.literal: He held the post of Erudite of the Imperial Academy, compiled the Imperial Diary, and concurrently served as Supervisor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He served as erudite of the Imperial Academy, compiled the imperial diary, and concurrently as supervisor in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 為還園賦，其辭甚美。

translations.literal: He composed the Rhapsody on Returning to the Garden; its language was very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Rhapsody on Returning to the Garden, a work of exceptional literary beauty.

sentences.zh: 正光中，京兆王西征，引為大行臺郎中，委以書記。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era, the Prince of Jingzhao campaigned west and brought him in as Director of the Grand Mobile Office, entrusting him with records.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era, when the Prince of Jingzhao marched west on campaign, he took Su on as director of the grand mobile office and entrusted him with all written records.

sentences.zh: 還，除尚書左中兵郎中，卒。

translations.literal: On return he was made Director of Central Arms in the Left Secretariat of the Ministry of Works and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was appointed director of central arms in the left secretariat of the Ministry of Works, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 肅性恭儉，不妄交遊，唯與崔勵、勵從兄鴻尤相親善。

translations.literal: Su by nature was respectful and frugal, not making friends rashly; only with Cui Li and Li's cousin Hong was he especially intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Su was by nature respectful and frugal and did not make friends lightly; only Cui Li and Li's cousin Hong were especially close to him.

sentences.zh: 所製文章多亡失，存者十餘卷。

translations.literal: The writings he composed were mostly lost; more than ten scrolls survive.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his writings have been lost; only a little more than ten scrolls survive.

sentences.zh: 邢臧，字子良，河間人，光祿少卿虬長孫也。

translations.literal: Xing Cang, style name Ziliang, was a man of Hejian and the eldest grandson of Vice Director of the Imperial Household Xing Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Cang, whose style was Ziliang, came from Hejian and was the eldest grandson of Vice Director of the Imperial Household Xing Qiu.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，早立操尚，博學有藻思。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he early established moral resolve, was broadly learned and had literary thought.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he early formed a strong moral character, was widely learned, and possessed a refined literary mind.

sentences.zh: 年二十一，神龜中，舉秀才，問策五條，考上第，為太學博士。

translations.literal: At twenty-one, in the Shengui era, he was recommended as a cultivated talent; on five policy questions he ranked at the top and was made Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-one, during the Shengui era, he was recommended as a cultivated talent; on five policy questions he placed at the top and was appointed erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 正光中，議立明堂，臧為裴頠一室之議，事雖不行，當時稱其理博。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era, when the Bright Hall was debated, Cang drafted Pei Zhi's one-room proposal; though the matter was not carried out, at the time his reasoning was praised as broad.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era, when the court debated building the Bright Hall, Cang drafted the one-room proposal associated with Pei Zhi; though the plan was not adopted, contemporaries praised the breadth of his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 出為本州中從事，雅為鄉情所附。

translations.literal: He went out as Central Assistant of his native province and was gracefully attached to by local sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as central assistant of his native province and was warmly supported by local opinion.

sentences.zh: 永安初，徵為金部郎中，以疾不赴，轉除東牟太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was summoned as Director of the Gold Bureau but did not go because of illness; he was transferred and made Administrator of Dongmou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was summoned as director of the gold bureau but declined because of illness; he was then transferred and appointed administrator of Dongmou.

sentences.zh: 時天下多事，在職少能廉白，臧獨清慎奉法，吏民愛之。

translations.literal: At the time the realm had many troubles; few in office could be pure and upright, but Cang alone was clear, cautious, and observant of law, and officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in turmoil, and few officials could remain honest and upright; Cang alone was scrupulous and law-abiding, and both clerks and common people admired him.

sentences.zh: 隴西李延寔，莊帝之舅，以太傅出除青州，啟臧為屬，領樂安內史，有惠政。

translations.literal: Li Yanshi of Longxi, the maternal uncle of Emperor Xiaozhuang, went out as Grand Tutor to Qingzhou, recommended Cang as aide, and had him lead as Interior Secretary of Le'an, with benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanshi of Longxi, Emperor Xiaozhuang's maternal uncle, left the capital as grand tutor to take up Qingzhou; he recommended Cang as his aide and had him serve concurrently as interior secretary of Le'an, where he governed with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 後除濮陽太守，尋加安東將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was made Administrator of Puyang and soon additionally given the title Pacifier of the East General.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed administrator of Puyang and soon given the additional title of pacifier of the east general.

sentences.zh: 臧和雅信厚，有長者之風，為時人所愛敬。

translations.literal: Cang was harmonious, refined, faithful, and generous, with the bearing of an elder, and was loved and respected by people of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Cang was gentle, refined, trustworthy, and generous, with the bearing of a man of mature virtue, and was loved and respected by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 為特進甄琛行狀，世稱其工。

translations.literal: He composed the conduct account for Special Advancement Zhen Chen, and the age praised its craftsmanship.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the conduct account for Zhen Chen, holder of special advancement, and contemporaries praised its craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 與裴敬憲、盧觀兄弟並結交分，曾共讀回文集，臧獨先通之。

translations.literal: With Pei Jingxian and the brothers Lu Guan he formed bonds of friendship; they once together read Hui's collected writings, and Cang alone first mastered them.
translations.idiomatic: He formed close friendships with Pei Jingxian and the brothers Lu Guan; they once read Feng Hui's collected writings together, and Cang alone mastered them first.

sentences.zh: 撰古來文章，并敍作者氏族，號曰文譜，未就，病卒，時賢悼惜之。

translations.literal: He compiled writings from antiquity to the present and also narrated authors' clans and surnames, calling it the Literary Genealogy; it was unfinished when he died of illness, and worthies of the time mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He was compiling writings from antiquity to his own day, with notes on each author's clan and lineage, under the title Literary Genealogy; he died of illness before finishing it, and leading men of the day deeply mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 其文筆凡百餘篇。

translations.literal: His literary pieces altogether numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: His literary pieces altogether numbered more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮北將軍、定州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Pacifier of the North General and Governor of Dingzhou, posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as pacifier of the north general and governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 子恕，涉學有識悟。

translations.literal: His son Shu was versed in learning and had understanding.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu was well read and showed keen understanding.

sentences.zh: 裴伯茂，河東人，司空中郎叔義第二子。

translations.literal: Pei Bomao was a man of Hedong and the second son of Central Adjutant in the Bureau of the Minister of Works, Shuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Bomao came from Hedong and was the second son of Shuyi, central adjutant in the Bureau of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 少有風望，學涉羣書，文藻富贍。

translations.literal: In youth he had bearing and reputation, learning traversed many books, and his literary ornament was rich and ample.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed presence and promise, ranged widely through many books, and wrote with rich literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: On leaving the cloth he was made Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On entering official service he was appointed court attendant.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、京兆王繼西討，引為鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: The Great General, Prince of Jingzhao, Ji, campaigned west and brought him in as Adjutant in the Armor Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the great general, Prince Ji of Jingzhao, marched west on campaign, he took Bomao on as adjutant in the armor bureau.

sentences.zh: 南討絳蜀陳雙熾，[5]為行臺長孫承業行臺郎中。

translations.literal: Campaigning south against Chen Shuangchi of Jiang and Shu, he served as Director of the Mobile Office for Changsun Chengye's mobile command.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Chen Shuangchi of Jiang and Shu, he served as director of the mobile office on Changsun Chengye's staff.

sentences.zh: 承業還京師，留伯茂仍知行臺事。

translations.literal: Chengye returned to the capital and left Bomao still to handle mobile office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengye returned to the capital, he left Bomao behind to continue managing mobile-office affairs.

sentences.zh: 以平薛鳳賢等賞平陽伯。

translations.literal: For pacifying Xue Fengxian and others he was rewarded with the title Marquis of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Xue Fengxian and others he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 再遷散騎常侍，典起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and supervised the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and put in charge of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，出帝兄子廣平王贊盛選賓僚，以伯茂為文學，後加中軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, the Deposed Emperor's elder brother's son, Prince of Guangping, Zan, greatly selected guest officials and made Bomao literary aide; later he was additionally given Central Army Great General.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, Zan, Prince of Guangping and nephew of the deposed emperor, carefully selected his staff and appointed Bomao literary aide; Bomao was later given the additional title of central army great general.

sentences.zh: 伯茂好飲酒，頗涉疏傲，久不徙官，曾為豁情賦，其序略曰：「余攝養舛和，服餌寡術，自春徂夏，三嬰湊疾。

translations.literal: Bomao loved drinking wine and was rather given to negligence and arrogance; long he was not transferred in office. He once composed the Rhapsody on Open Feeling; its preface in brief says, "My regimen of nurture was out of harmony, and in taking medicines I had few techniques; from spring to summer, three times I was stricken with gathered illness.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao was fond of wine and rather careless and arrogant; for a long time he received no promotion. He once wrote the Rhapsody on Open Feeling; its preface reads in part, "My regimen was out of balance, and I had little skill in taking medicine; from spring through summer I was stricken three times by serious illness.

sentences.zh: 雖桐君上藥，有時致効；

translations.literal: Though the Superior Lord Tong's medicines sometimes took effect;
translations.idiomatic: Though the superior medicines of Lord Tong of the Divine Farmer sometimes helped;

sentences.zh: 而草木下性，實縈衿抱。

translations.literal: yet the lower nature of plants and trees truly bound my breast and embrace.
translations.idiomatic: yet the humble nature of herbs and plants still weighed on my heart.

sentences.zh: 故復究覽莊生，具體齊物，物我兩忘，是非俱遣，斯人之達，吾所師焉。

translations.literal: Therefore I again thoroughly examined Master Zhuang, embodied the Equalization of Things, forgot both thing and self, dismissed both right and wrong—such a person's attainment is what I take as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: So I turned again to Master Zhuang, took to heart the Equalization of Things, forgot both self and world, and set aside all distinctions of right and wrong; such attainment is the master I follow.

sentences.zh: 故作是賦，所以託名豁情，寄之風謠矣。

translations.literal: Therefore I composed this rhapsody, thereby entrusting the name Open Feeling and lodging it in wind songs.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this rhapsody, taking the name Open Feeling and lodging my mood in verse.

sentences.zh: 」天平初遷鄴，又為遷都賦，文多不載。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Tianping the capital moved to Ye; he also composed the Rhapsody on Moving the Capital, but most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: " At the beginning of the Tianping era, when the capital moved to Ye, he also wrote a Rhapsody on Moving the Capital, but most of the text is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 二年，因內宴，伯茂侮慢殿中尚書、章武王景哲，景哲遂申啟，稱：「伯茂棄其本列，與監同行；

translations.literal: In the second year, at an inner banquet, Bomao insulted and slighted Director within the Palace, Prince of Zhangwu, Jingzhe; Jingzhe then submitted a report, saying, "Bomao abandoned his proper rank and walked alongside a supervisor;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, at an inner court banquet, Bomao insulted Jingzhe, director within the palace and Prince of Zhangwu; Jingzhe then submitted a memorial saying, "Bomao abandoned his proper station and walked alongside a supervisor;

sentences.zh: 以梨擊案，傍汙冠服；

translations.literal: struck the table with a pear, and beside him soiled cap and robe;
translations.idiomatic: struck the table with a pear and splattered those beside him, soiling their caps and robes;

sentences.zh: 禁庭之內，令人挈衣。

translations.literal: within the forbidden court, had someone carry off clothing.
translations.idiomatic: and within the forbidden precinct of the palace had someone carry off another man's garment.

sentences.zh: 」詔付所司，後竟無坐。

translations.literal: " An edict handed the matter to the responsible office, but in the end there was no conviction.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict referred the matter to the appropriate office, but in the end he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 伯茂先出後其伯仲規，與兄景融別居。

translations.literal: Bomao was born after his elder and younger brother Gui and lived separately from his elder brother Jingrong.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao was born after his brothers Gui and lived apart from his elder brother Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 景融貧窘，伯茂了無賑恤，殆同行路，世以此貶薄之。

translations.literal: Jingrong was poor and straitened; Bomao had no relief or support for him, almost like passing on the road, and the age for this belittled and slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong was poor and in distress, yet Bomao gave him no help at all, behaving almost like a stranger; contemporaries despised him for this.

sentences.zh: 卒年三十九，知舊歎惜焉。

translations.literal: He died at age thirty-nine, and friends and old acquaintances sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-nine, and friends and acquaintances mourned him.

sentences.zh: 伯茂末年劇飲不已，乃至傷性，多有愆失。

translations.literal: In his later years Bomao drank heavily without cease, even to harming his nature, and had many faults and lapses.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Bomao drank heavily without stop, even harming his health, and committed many lapses.

sentences.zh: 未亡前數日，忽云：「吾得密信，將被收掩。

translations.literal: Several days before his death he suddenly said, "I have received a secret message that I am about to be seized and arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Several days before his death he suddenly said, "I have received a secret report that I am about to be arrested.

sentences.zh: 」乃與婦乘車西逃避。

translations.literal: " He then rode west in a carriage with his wife to flee and hide.
translations.idiomatic: " He then fled west in a carriage with his wife.

sentences.zh: 後因顧指壁中，言有官人追逐，其妻方知其病。

translations.literal: Later he turned and pointed at the wall, saying officials were pursuing him; only then did his wife know he was ill.
translations.idiomatic: Later he turned and pointed at the wall, saying that officials were pursuing him; only then did his wife realize he was delirious.

sentences.zh: 卒後，殯於家園，友人常景、李渾、王元景、盧元明、魏季景、李騫等十許人於墓傍置酒設祭，哀哭涕泣，一飲一酹曰：「裴中書魂而有靈，知吾曹也。

translations.literal: After his death he was encoffined in the family garden; some ten friends—Chang Jing, Li Hun, Wang Yuanjing, Lu Yuanming, Wei Jijing, Li Qian, and others—set out wine and made offerings beside the tomb, weeping in grief with tears, and with each drink and libation said, "Vice Director Pei, if your soul has spirit, know us.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was buried in the family estate; some ten friends, including Chang Jing, Li Hun, Wang Yuanjing, Lu Yuanming, Wei Jijing, and Li Qian, set out wine and offerings beside the tomb, weeping as they drank and poured libations, saying, "Vice Director Pei, if your spirit hears us, know that we are here.

sentences.zh: 」乃各賦詩一篇。

translations.literal: " Each then composed one poem.
translations.idiomatic: " Each then composed a poem in his memory.

sentences.zh: 李騫以魏收亦與之友，寄以示收。

translations.literal: Li Qian, since Wei Shou was also his friend, sent them to show Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qian sent the poems to Wei Shou, who had also been Bomao's friend.

sentences.zh: 收時在晉陽，乃同其作，論敍伯茂，其十字云：「臨風想玄度，對酒思公榮。

translations.literal: Shou was then at Jinyang, and joined in their composition, narrating Bomao; its ten characters said: "Facing the wind one thinks of Xuandu; facing wine one thinks of Gongrong."
translations.idiomatic: Shou was then at Jinyang and contributed his own piece on Bomao; its ten-character line read, "Facing the wind I think of Xu Xuan; over wine I think of Liu Gongrong."

sentences.zh: 」時人以伯茂性侮傲，謂收詩頗得事實。

translations.literal: " People of the time, because Bomao's nature was arrogant and insulting, said Shou's poem rather hit the facts.
translations.idiomatic: " Because Bomao's nature was haughty and overbearing, contemporaries said Shou's lines captured him well.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、衞將軍、度支尚書、雍州刺史，重贈吏部尚書，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds, Guard General, Minister of Revenue, Inspector of Yongzhou; again posthumously made Minister of the Personnel, posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds, Guard General, and Minister of Revenue with concurrent duty as Inspector of Yongzhou; later posthumously promoted to Minister of the Personnel with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 伯茂曾撰晉書，竟未能成。

translations.literal: Bomao once compiled a History of Jin; in the end he was unable to finish it.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao once undertook a History of Jin but never completed it.

sentences.zh: 無子，兄景融以第二子孝才繼。

translations.literal: He had no son; elder brother Jingrong had his second son Xiaocai succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his elder brother Jingrong had his second son Xiaocai succeed him.

sentences.zh: 邢昕，字子明，河間人，尚書巒弟偉之子。

translations.literal: Xing Xin, styled Ziming, a man of Hejian, was son of Wei, younger brother of Luan, Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Xin, styled Ziming, was a native of Hejian and the son of Wei, younger brother of Minister Luan.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，見愛於祖母李氏。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was cherished by his grandmother Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he was doted on by his grandmother, Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 好學，早有才情。

translations.literal: He loved study and showed literary talent early.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and displayed literary talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤以車騎大將軍開府討關中，以子明為東閤祭酒，委以文翰。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin served as Cavalry General-in-Chief with an open headquarters to campaign against Guanzhong, he made Ziming Eastern Pavillion Libationer and entrusted him with literary documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin opened a field headquarters as Cavalry General-in-Chief to campaign in Guanzhong, he appointed Ziming Eastern Pavillion Libationer and entrusted him with official correspondence.

sentences.zh: 在軍解褐盪寇將軍，累遷太尉記室參軍。

translations.literal: In the army he doffed his plain robe as Campaign General Who Quells Banditry; he was promoted repeatedly to Army Aide of Record to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: While on campaign he entered official service as Campaign General Who Quells Banditry and was promoted step by step to Army Aide of Record to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李神儁奏昕修起居注。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun, Minister of the Personnel, memorialized that Xin should compile the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, Minister of the Personnel, memorialized that Xin should compile the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，除中書侍郎，加平東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, with additional titles as General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat with the additional ranks of General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時言冒竊官級，為中尉所劾，免官，乃為述躬賦。

translations.literal: At the time it was said he had usurped others' ranks; the Commandant of Justice impeached him, he was dismissed, and he then wrote the "Fu on Embodying Oneself."
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then claimed he had fraudulently taken another's rank; impeached by the Commandant of Justice, he was dismissed from office and wrote the "Fu on Embodying Oneself."

sentences.zh: 未幾，受詔與祕書監常景典儀注事。

translations.literal: Before long, he received an edict jointly with Chang Jing, Director of the Palace Library, to oversee ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received an edict to oversee ritual regulations together with Chang Jing, Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 出帝行釋奠禮，昕與校書郎裴伯茂等俱為錄義。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor performed the Confucian sacrifice, Xin together with Collator Pei Bomao and others all served as recorders of the exposition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor performed the Confucian temple sacrifice, Xin together with Collator Pei Bomao and others served as recorders of the rites.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，昕入為侍讀，與溫子昇、魏收參掌文詔。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxi, Xin entered court as Reader-in-Waiting, and with Wen Zisheng and Wei Shou jointly managed edicts and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongxi era, Xin entered court as Reader-in-Waiting and, together with Wen Zisheng and Wei Shou, shared responsibility for edicts and imperial documents.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴，乃歸河間。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Ye, he returned to Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved to Ye, he returned to Hejian.

sentences.zh: 天平初，與侍中從叔子才、魏季景、魏收同徵赴都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was summoned to the capital together with Palace Attendant and clan uncle Zicai, Wei Jijing, and Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was summoned to the capital together with Palace Attendant and paternal uncle Zicai, Wei Jijing, and Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 尋還鄉里。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned home.

sentences.zh: 既而復徵。

translations.literal: Afterward he was summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again not long after.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍使兼散騎常侍劉孝儀等來朝貢，詔昕兼正員郎迎於境上。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Yan's envoys, including Vice Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds Liu Xiaoyi, came to court with tribute; an edict appointed Xin Acting Regular Gentleman to welcome them at the border.
translations.idiomatic: At that time envoys from Xiao Yan, including Vice Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds Liu Xiaoyi, came bearing tribute; an edict made Xin Acting Regular Gentleman to receive them at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 司徒孫騰引為中郎。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Sun Teng recommended him as Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Sun Teng recommended him as Palace Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 尋除通直常侍，加中軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Service, with the additional rank of General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Service with the additional rank of General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 既有才藻，兼長几案。

translations.literal: He had both literary talent and skill at desk work.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed both literary brilliance and administrative competence at the desk.

sentences.zh: 自孝昌之後，天下多務，世人競以吏工取達，文學大衰。

translations.literal: From Xiaochang onward the realm was burdened with tasks, and people in the world competed to advance through bureaucratic craft, while letters and learning greatly declined.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiaochang era the empire was overwhelmed with affairs, and men competed to rise through bureaucratic skill while literary learning sharply declined.

sentences.zh: 司州中從事宋遊道以公斷見知，時與昕嘲謔。

translations.literal: Song Youdao, secretariat aide of the provincial inspectorate of Sizhou, was known for fair judgment; at the time he and Xin would banter and joke.
translations.idiomatic: Song Youdao, Secretariat Aide of Sizhou, was known for fair-minded decisiveness; he and Xin often exchanged witty taunts.

sentences.zh: 昕謂之曰：「世事同知文學外。

translations.literal: Xin said to him: "In worldly affairs one must know what lies outside literature."
translations.idiomatic: Xin told him, "In worldly affairs one must know what lies beyond letters."

sentences.zh: 」遊道有慚色。

translations.literal: " Youdao showed an ashamed countenance.
translations.idiomatic: " Youdao flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 興和中，以本官副李象使於蕭衍。

translations.literal: In Xinghe, with his existing office he served as deputy to Li Xiang on a mission to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xinghe era he served as deputy to Li Xiang on a mission to Xiao Yan, retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 昕好忤物，人謂之牛。

translations.literal: Xin loved to go against others; people called him the Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was fond of crossing others; people nicknamed him the Ox.

sentences.zh: 是行也，談者謂之牛象鬬於江南。

translations.literal: On this journey, gossips called it an Ox and Elephant fighting south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: On that mission, observers quipped that an ox and an elephant were fighting south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王攝選，擬昕為司徒右長史，未奏，遇疾卒，士友悲之。

translations.literal: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi acted as regent in selections, he proposed Xin as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; before the memorial was submitted, Xin fell ill and died, and gentlemen mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi oversaw appointments, he proposed Xin as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; before the nomination reached the throne, Xin fell ill and died, to the grief of his peers.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍、都官尚書、冀州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Cavalry General-in-Chief, Minister of Justice, Inspector of Jizhou, posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Cavalry General-in-Chief, Minister of Justice, and Inspector of Jizhou with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 所著文章，自有集錄。

translations.literal: His literary writings were collected in their own anthology.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were gathered in a collected anthology.

sentences.zh: 溫子昇，字鵬舉，自云太原人，晉大將軍嶠之後也。

translations.literal: Wen Zisheng, styled Pengju, claimed himself a man of Taiyuan and a descendant of the Jin general Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zisheng, styled Pengju, claimed descent from Taiyuan and from the Jin general Jiao.

sentences.zh: 世居江左。

translations.literal: His clan had long dwelt south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived south of the Yangtze for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖恭之，劉義隆彭城王義康戶曹，避難歸國，家于濟陰冤句，因為其郡縣人焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gongzhi was a clerk in the household of Liu Yikang's Prince of Pengcheng; fleeing hardship he returned to the north, and the family settled in Yuanqu, Jiyin, thus becoming natives of that commandery and county.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gongzhi had served as a clerk in the household of Liu Yikang's Prince of Pengcheng; fleeing turmoil he returned to the north, and the family settled at Yuanqu in Jiyin, thus becoming natives of that district.

sentences.zh: 家世寒素。

translations.literal: The family for generations was poor and plain.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had been poor and of modest standing.

sentences.zh: 父暉，兗州左將軍府長史，行濟陰郡事。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Army Aide of Record to the Left General of Yanzhou and acted as Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was Army Aide of Record to the Left General of Yanzhou and concurrently administered Jiyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 子昇初受學於崔靈恩、劉蘭，精勤，以夜繼晝，晝夜不倦。

translations.literal: Zisheng first studied under Cui Lin'en and Liu Lan, diligent and exacting, continuing night into day, day and night never weary.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng first studied under Cui Lin'en and Liu Lan, applying himself with such zeal that he worked on through the night into the day without ever tiring.

sentences.zh: 長乃博覽百家，文章清婉。

translations.literal: When grown he broadly read the hundred schools; his compositions were pure and graceful.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he read widely among the hundred schools; his writing was clear and graceful.

sentences.zh: 為廣陽王淵賤客，在馬坊教諸奴子書。

translations.literal: He was a lowly retainer of Prince Guangyang of Yuan Yuan; in the horse stables he taught the slave boys to write.
translations.idiomatic: He was a low-ranking retainer in the household of Prince Yuan of Guangyang, teaching the stable boys to write in the horse quarters.

sentences.zh: 作侯山祠堂碑文，常景見而善之，故詣淵謝之。

translations.literal: He composed an inscription for the Hou Mountain temple; Chang Jing saw it and approved, and therefore went to Yuan to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote an inscription for the Hou Mountain shrine; Chang Jing read it, admired it, and went to Yuan to express his thanks on Zisheng's behalf.

sentences.zh: 景曰：「頃見溫生。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Recently I saw Master Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "I have just seen Master Wen."

sentences.zh: 」淵怪問之，景曰：「溫生是大才士。

translations.literal: " Yuan asked in surprise; Jing said: "Master Wen is a great talent in letters."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan asked in surprise; Jing said, "Master Wen is a man of great literary talent."

sentences.zh: 」淵由是稍知之。

translations.literal: " Yuan thereby gradually came to know him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan thereby came to know him somewhat.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，中尉、東平王匡博召辭人，以充御史，同時射策者八百餘人，子昇與盧仲宣、孫搴等二十四人為高第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping, the Commandant of Justice, Prince Kuang of Dongping, broadly summoned men of letters to fill the Censorate; at the same time over eight hundred took the policy examination; Zisheng with Lu Zhongxuan, Sun Qian, and twenty-two others placed in the top tier.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiping, Prince Kuang of Dongping, Commandant of Justice, summoned literary men broadly to fill the Censorate; over eight hundred candidates took the policy examination at once, and Zisheng with Lu Zhongxuan, Sun Qian, and twenty-two others ranked in the top tier.

sentences.zh: 於時預選者爭相引決，匡使子昇當之，皆受屈而去。

translations.literal: At the time those who had been pre-selected vied to withdraw; Kuang had Zisheng face them, and all yielded and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had been shortlisted then vied to withdraw rather than face him; Kuang had Zisheng stand against them, and each yielded and left.

sentences.zh: 搴謂人曰：「朝來靡旗亂轍者，皆子昇逐北。

sentences.zh: 」遂補御史，時年二十二。

translations.literal: All literary drafts of the Censorate were by Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: All literary drafts in the Censorate were Zisheng's work.

sentences.zh: 以憂去任，服闋，還為朝請。

translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the central government, but Shenjun memorialized to retain him and not let him go.

translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he returned to the capital.

translations.idiomatic: His fame for talent then grew still greater.

translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was slain by Ge Rong, Zisheng too was seized and detained.

translations.idiomatic: Heluo Xing, a subordinate commander under Rong and an old acquaintance of Zisheng, secretly escorted him with several dozen horsemen until he reached Jizhou.

translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, Li Kai grasped his hand and said, "You have come through alive—enough to make Yifu blush for his character."

translations.idiomatic: " From then on he lost all desire for office, shut his door to read, and honed his mind without cease.

translations.idiomatic: Tianmu was furious and memorialized to replace him.

translations.literal: The Emperor Zhuang said: "Men of talent in this age number but a few—how can we for this dismiss him outright?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang said, "Men of talent in our age number only a handful—how can we for this dismiss him outright?"

sentences.zh: 」乃寢其奏。

translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was then shelved.

translations.idiomatic: When Tianmu was about to campaign against Xing Gao, he summoned Zisheng to accompany him; Zisheng did not dare answer.

translations.idiomatic: Tianmu told others, "I wish to employ his talent—would I harbor old resentment?"

sentences.zh: 今復不來，便須南走越，北走胡耳！

translations.literal: If you do not come now, you must flee south to Yue or north to the barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: If you still do not come, you will have to flee south to Yue or north to the barbarians!

translations.literal: " Zisheng had no choice but to see him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zisheng had no choice but to present himself.

translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional rank of General Who Subdues Waves and made Gentleman of the Circuit Headquarters; Tianmu prized him deeply.

translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Tianmu summoned Zisheng and asked, "Do you mean to head straight for the capital, or follow me north across the river?"

translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The sovereign, because Tiger Cage was lost, has been reduced to this plight."

translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao has only just entered; the people's hearts are not yet settled; if you march now to attack him, you will surely win without fighting.

translations.literal: If Your Highness recovers the capital, welcomes back the great carriage—this is a deed of Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness recovers the capital and welcomes back the imperial carriage, that will be a feat like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, many whom Hao had appointed as envoys were dismissed, but Zisheng again became Drafting Officer.

translations.idiomatic: Tianmu often told Zisheng, "I regret not having followed your earlier plan."

translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Gentleman while still serving as Drafting Officer.

translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor killed Erzhu Rong, Zisheng took part in the plot; the amnesty edict of that hour was in Zisheng's words.

translations.idiomatic: Rong entered the inner quarters, met Zisheng, seized the edict and asked what document it was; Zisheng's expression did not change as he answered, "An imperial order."

translations.literal: Rong did not look at it.
translations.idiomatic: Rong did not read it.

translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Zisheng feared calamity and hid himself.

translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi he served as Reader-in-Waiting with concurrent duty as Drafting Officer, General Who Guards the South, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Tassel; he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds and Great General of the Central Army, and later headed the senior clan scorer for his native province.

translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan had Zhang Gao copy Zisheng's writings, which circulated beyond the Yangtze.

translations.idiomatic: Yan praised him, saying, "Cao Zhi and Lu Ji are reborn in the northern lands."

translations.literal: "I regret that among my men of letters the count has been exhausted by the cycle of calamity."
translations.idiomatic: "I only regret that among my literary men fortune has been broken by repeated calamity."

translations.idiomatic: " Fu Biao, Administrator of Yangxia, on a mission to the Tuyuhun, saw several scrolls at the ruler's bedside—they were writings of Zisheng.

translations.literal: Prince Huiye of Jiyin once said: "Among men of letters south of the Yangtze, in Song there were Yan Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun, in Liang there were Shen Yue and Ren Fang; our Zisheng suffices to tread upon Yan and crush Xie, swallow Ren and spit out Shen."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huiye of Jiyin once said, "Among literati south of the Yangtze, Song had Yan Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun, Liang had Shen Yue and Ren Fang; our Zisheng is enough to stride over Yan and trample Xie, encompass Ren and surpass Shen."

sentences.zh: 」楊遵彥作文德論，以為古今辭人皆負才遺行，澆薄險忌，唯邢子才、王元景、溫子昇彬彬有德素。

translations.literal: " Yang Zunyan wrote the "Discourse on Literary Virtue," holding that men of letters ancient and modern all bore talent yet cast off conduct, shallow, thin, treacherous, and jealous—only Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, and Wen Zisheng were refined and possessed virtue and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyan wrote the "Discourse on Literary Virtue," arguing that writers of every age bore talent yet abandoned proper conduct—shallow, base, treacherous, and jealous—yet only Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, and Wen Zisheng were refined and possessed genuine virtue.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王引子昇為大將軍府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiang of Qi summoned Zisheng as Adviser of the Grand General's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang of Qi summoned Zisheng as Adviser of the Grand General's Headquarters.

translations.idiomatic: Zisheng had previously served as Secretariat Gentleman and once went to Xiao Yan's guesthouse to receive the state letter; finding his bearing inadequate, he told others, "Poems are easy to write; striking presence is hard to manage."

translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Jin, a retainer at Wenxiang's residence, said, "Everyone ought to congratulate."

translations.idiomatic: " [Editorial note 8] They urged Zisheng to help draft the presentation speech.

translations.idiomatic: Zisheng hesitated for some time, then put forward Lu Cao in his stead.

translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Jin, Liu Siyi, Xun Ji, and the others rose in revolt, Prince Wenxiang suspected that Zisheng had known of their conspiracy.

translations.literal: He had just had him compose the stele text for King Xianwu; once it was finished, he starved him in the Jinyang prison; eating tattered clothes he died; his corpse was cast by the roadside; his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: He was just then having him write the inscription for King Xianwu. When it was done, he left him to starve in the Jinyang prison; he died gnawing rotten rags. His body was thrown by the road, and his entire household was seized.

sentences.zh: 太尉長史宋遊道收葬之，又為集其文筆為三十五卷。

translations.literal: Song Youdao, Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant, gathered and buried him, and also compiled his writings into thirty-five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Song Youdao, Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant, recovered his body for burial and also collected his literary works into thirty-five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子昇外恬靜，與物無競，言有準的，不妄毀譽，而內深險。

translations.literal: Outwardly Zisheng was calm and still, competing with nothing; his words had their mark; he did not rashly praise or blame—yet inwardly he was deeply treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng appeared outwardly serene and uncontentious; his speech was measured, and he did not praise or revile rashly—yet within he was profoundly cunning.

sentences.zh: 事故之際，好預其間，所以終致禍敗。

translations.literal: At times of incidents he liked to take part in them; and so he ultimately met calamity and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When troubles arose, he liked to thrust himself into them—hence his final fall to ruin.

sentences.zh: 又撰永安記三卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled Records of Yong'an in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Records of Yong'an in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

translations.literal: The historiographer says: What the men of old prized in undying fame was chiefly that their words still survived, further joined with literary talent and name; that they should be honored and eminent is indeed fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: What the ancients valued in fame that would not perish was, above all, that their words still lived—and when literary talent and reputation were added besides, eminence and honor were only as they ought to be.

sentences.zh: 自餘或位下人微，居常亦何能自達。

translations.literal: As for the rest, whether of low rank or slight personage—in ordinary life how could they make themselves known?
translations.idiomatic: As for all the others, of humble station or slight consequence—what chance had they to win notice in their daily lives?

sentences.zh: 及其靈蛇可握，天網俱頓，並編緗素，咸貫儒林，雖其位可下，其身可殺，千載之後，貴賤一焉。

translations.literal: Yet when the spiritual serpent could be grasped and the heavenly net all slackened, all were compiled on silk plain, all pierced the Confucian forest; though their positions might be brought low and their persons might be killed, a thousand years hence noble and base are one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when fortune turned and restraint fell away, their works were all set down on silk and paper and all entered the grove of scholars. Though rank might be stripped from them and their lives taken, a thousand years on, high and low alike are one.

sentences.zh: 非此道也，孰云能致。

translations.literal: Without this path, who could say they could attain it?
translations.idiomatic: By any other means, who could have achieved the same?

sentences.zh: 凡百士子，可不務乎！

translations.literal: Every scholar—ought they not devote themselves to it!
translations.idiomatic: Every man of letters—should he not strive for this?

translations.idiomatic: " Yet this volume lacks entries for Lu Zhongxuan and Pei Zhuangbo. Later editors must have meant to supply biographies listed in the table of contents but failed to do so: Zhongxuan and Zhuangbo were merely appended to their elder brothers' biographies, not given independent entries, so the table of contents did not list them—and the supplement was never made.

sentences.zh: 靈均逐楚著嘉禍之章按「嘉禍」未見所出，楚辭九章橘頌：「后皇嘉樹，橘徠服兮。

translations.literal: Lingjun followed Chu, composing the chapter on auspicious calamity—Commentary: "Jia huo" is nowhere attested; Songs of Chu, Nine Chapters, Ode to the Orange: "O sovereign's noble tree, the orange has come to take root here.
translations.idiomatic: "Qu Yuan followed Chu into exile and composed the chapter on 'auspicious calamity'"—Commentary: The phrase "Jia huo" (auspicious calamity) has no known source. The Songs of Chu, "Ode to the Orange" in the Nine Pieces, reads: "O sovereign's noble tree, the orange has come to take root here."

sentences.zh: 」疑「嘉禍」乃「嘉橘」之訛。

translations.literal: " Suspect "Jia huo" is error for "Jia ju" (noble orange).
translations.idiomatic: " The reading "Jia huo" is probably a corruption of "Jia ju" (noble orange).

sentences.zh: 中山王將之部諸本無「王」字，旁注「闕」。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhongshan about to go to his prefecture—in various editions the character "prince" is absent; marginal note "lacuna".
translations.idiomatic: "When the Prince of Zhongshan was about to depart for his commandery"—several editions omit the word "prince," with a marginal note reading "lacuna."

sentences.zh: 通志卷一七六裴敬憲傳作「王」，冊府卷八三九

translations.literal: Comprehensive Records, scroll 176, Biography of Pei Jingxian, has "prince"; Cefu Yuangui, scroll 839
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Records, volume 176, biography of Pei Jingxian, reads "prince." The Cefu Yuangui, scroll 839

sentences.zh: 〈九九六０頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 9960〉

sentences.zh: 此句作「中山鎮部」。

translations.literal: this sentence reads "Zhongshan garrisoned district".
translations.idiomatic: renders this line as "Zhongshan garrisoned the district."

sentences.zh: 按卷一九南安王楨附中山王熙傳云：「始熙之鎮鄴也，知友才學之士略裴敬憲等咸餞於河梁，賦詩告別。

translations.literal: According to this book, scroll 19, Nan'an Wang Zhen with attached Biography of Prince of Zhongshan Xi, says: "When Xi first took up garrison at Ye, learned friends and men of talent and letters including Pei Jingxian all held a farewell banquet at River Bridge, composing poems to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei, volume 19, biography of Prince Nan'an Zhen with the attached biography of Prince Zhongshan Xi, states: "When Xi first took up his post at Ye, men of talent and learning among his friends, including Pei Jingxian, all saw him off with a feast at River Bridge and composed farewell poems."

sentences.zh: 」「中山」下脫「王」字無疑，今據補。

translations.literal: " Under "Zhongshan" the character "prince" is certainly missing; now supplemented accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " The omission of "prince" after "Zhongshan" is certain; the character is restored here.

sentences.zh: 冊府「鎮」字，當亦有因，疑此句本作「中山王鎮鄴，將之部」。

translations.literal: Cefu's character "garrison" must also have reason; suspect the original sentence read "Prince of Zhongshan garrisoned Ye, about to go to his district".
translations.idiomatic: The Cefu's word "garrison" must have its own rationale; the original line was probably "When the Prince of Zhongshan was garrisoning Ye and about to depart for his commandery."

sentences.zh: 冊府所據本「鄴」訛「部」，和下「將之部」重出不辭，遂刪三字。

translations.literal: The edition Cefu drew on had "Ye" wrongly as "district"; with the following "about to go to his district" it would redundantly repeat and be ungrammatical, so three characters were deleted.
translations.idiomatic: In the edition the Cefu drew upon, Ye was miscopied as bu (district); combined with the following phrase about to go to his commandery, the result was redundant and awkward, so three characters were dropped.

sentences.zh: 永興三年按永興乃拓跋嗣年號

translations.literal: Third year of Yongxing—Commentary: Yongxing is the era name of Tuoba Si
translations.idiomatic: "In the third year of Yongxing"—Commentary: Yongxing was an era name of Tuoba Si (Emperor Daowu)

sentences.zh: 〈四０九－四一三〉
，遠在其前，元脩雖於太昌元年

translations.literal: , far before that time; though Yuan Xiu in the first year of Taichang
translations.idiomatic: , long before the relevant period. Yuan Xiu, it is true, in the first year of Taichang

sentences.zh: 〈五三二〉
十二月改永興，即在此月改永熙，並無三年。

translations.literal: in the twelfth month changed the era name to Yongxing, yet in that same month changed it to Yongxi—there was no third year.
translations.idiomatic: changed his era name to Yongxing in the twelfth month—and in that same month changed it again to Yongxi. There never was a "third year" of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 北史卷三八裴駿附敬憲傳同作「永興」，而下文其弟莊伯傳，稱「永安三年，贈通直散騎侍郎」。

translations.literal: Northern History, scroll 38, Pei Jun attached Jingxian biography likewise has "Yongxing", while below in his brother Zhuangbo's biography it says "third year of Yong'an, posthumously enfeoffed as Regular Attendant in the Direct Office of the Palace Guard Cavalry".
translations.idiomatic: The Northern History, volume 38, in the biography of Pei Jun with the attached biography of Jingxian, likewise reads "Yongxing," yet the biography of his brother Zhuangbo below says, "In the third year of Yong'an, posthumously appointed Regular Palace Gentleman in Direct Service."

sentences.zh: 兄弟當是同年追贈，這裏「永興」乃「永安」之訛。

translations.literal: The brothers were probably posthumously honored the same year; here "Yongxing" is error for "Yong'an".
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were probably granted posthumous honors in the same year; here "Yongxing" is a corruption of "Yong'an."

sentences.zh: 南討絳蜀陳雙熾通志卷一七六裴伯茂傳「南」作「及」。

translations.literal: Southern campaign against Jiang and Shu, Chen Shuang's revolt—Comprehensive Records, scroll 176, Biography of Pei Bomao, reads "south" as "and".
translations.idiomatic: A southern campaign against Jiang, Shu, and Chen Shuang's uprising—the Comprehensive Records, volume 176, biography of Pei Bomao, reads nan (south) as ji (and).

sentences.zh: 按絳在洛陽西北，不得云「南討」，疑作「及」是。

translations.literal: According to Jiang is northwest of Luoyang; one cannot say "southern campaign"; suspect writing "and" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang lies northwest of Luoyang, so a "southern campaign" makes no sense; "and" is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 還為朝請通志卷一七六溫子昇傳「朝請」上有「奉」字。

translations.literal: Returned to Court Attendant—Comprehensive Records, scroll 176, Biography of Wen Zisheng, has "receive" before "Court Attendant".
translations.idiomatic: Returned as Court Attendant—the Comprehensive Records, volume 176, biography of Wen Zisheng, has the character feng (serve or receive) before Court Attendant.

sentences.zh: 疑當有此字，但也可能是簡稱，今不補。

translations.literal: Suspect the character should be there, but it may also be an abbreviation; not supplemented now.
translations.idiomatic: The extra character may well belong, but it may also be an abbreviated form; no emendation is made here.

sentences.zh: 於是還省諸本及北史卷八三「省」作「員」，通志卷一七六作「省」。

translations.literal: Then returned to the Secretariat—in various editions and Northern History, scroll 83, "secretariat" is "staff officer"; Comprehensive Records, scroll 176, has "secretariat".
translations.idiomatic: Then returned to the Secretariat—in various editions and Northern History, volume 83, sheng (secretariat) is written as yuan (staff officer); the Comprehensive Records, volume 176, has sheng.

sentences.zh: 按上云：「被徵赴省」，故下云「還省」，「還員」不可通，今據改。

translations.literal: According to above it says "summoned to the Secretariat", so below "returned to Secretariat"—"returned to staff officer" does not parse; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the text reads that he was summoned to the Secretariat, so the following phrase must be returned to the Secretariat; huan yuan makes no sense. The reading sheng is adopted.

sentences.zh: 文襄館客元僅曰諸人當賀按何事當賀，敍述不明，疑「文襄」下有脫文。

translations.literal: Wenxiang's lodge client Yuan Jin said everyone should congratulate—Commentary: what occasion to congratulate is unclear, narrative is obscure, suspect text missing after "Wenxiang".
translations.idiomatic: "Yuan Jin, a retainer at Wenxiang's residence, said, 'Everyone ought to congratulate'"—Commentary: what there was to celebrate is nowhere made clear; the account is muddled. Text may be missing after "Wenxiang."

sentences.zh: 又「元僅」當作「元瑾」。

translations.literal: Also "Yuan Jin" (僅) should be "Yuan Jin" (瑾).
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yuan Jin written with the character jin (merely) should read Yuan Jin written with the character jin (gem).

sentences.zh: 瑾謀殺高澄，事見本書卷一二孝靜紀末、卷一四華山王鷙附子大器傳，北史卷六齊文襄紀，北齊書卷四七宋遊道傳，都作「瑾」。

translations.literal: Jin plotted to kill Gao Cheng; the affair is in this book, scroll 12, end of Emperor Xiaojing's annals, scroll 14, Huashan Wang Zhi with attached son Daqi biography, Northern History, scroll 6, Qi Wenxiang annals, Northern Qi Book, scroll 47, Song Youdao biography—all write "Jin" (瑾).
translations.idiomatic: Jin conspired to assassinate Gao Cheng; the episode appears in this book, volume 12 (end of the annals of Emperor Xiaojing), volume 14 (biography of Prince Huashan Zhi, with the attached biography of his son Daqi), Northern History, volume 6 (annals of Prince Wenxiang of Qi), and Northern Qi History, volume 47 (biography of Song Youdao)—all of which write the name with the character jin meaning gem.
